caption: Supplementary Fig. 2 | SOZ localization of raw and group-event-filtered interictal HFO burden. A, Subject-level receiver operating characteristic curves for distinguishing clinically labelled seizure onset zone (SOZ) from non-SOZ contacts using contact-wise group-event-filtered high-frequency oscillation (HFO) burden in the Yuquan (20 patients) and Epilepsiae (15 patients) cohorts; grey lines denote individual patients, coloured lines the cohort mean, shading the s.e.m., and inset points the patient-level area under the curve (AUC), with the black line indicating the mean. Mean AUC was 0.873 in Yuquan and 0.955 in Epilepsiae. B, Paired patient-level AUC before (Raw) and after restricting refined HFO detections to accepted population-event windows (Synchronized); bars and black horizontal lines indicate cohort means, and points joined by lines denote paired patients (Yuquan, 0.837 versus 0.873; Epilepsiae, 0.939 versus 0.955). Statistical significance was assessed using a two-sided paired Wilcoxon test; *P < 0.05; n.s., P ≥ 0.05.

panel_a.question: Does synchronized/refined interictal HFO burden distinguish clinical SOZ from non-SOZ contacts within subjects?

yuquan.curve_band: SEM across subject ROC curves after interpolation to 201 FPR points

epilepsiae.curve_band: SEM across subject ROC curves after interpolation to 201 FPR points

panel_a.auc_inset: one dot per subject; black bar is subject-mean AUC

panel_b.question: Does restricting raw HFO detections to accepted group-event windows improve subject-level SOZ AUC?
panel_b.test: two-sided paired Wilcoxon, matching the accepted SOZ validation producer
panel_b.terminology: Synchronized = refined HFO count inside accepted group-event windows; identical to the current _refineGpu event-count artifact.
